name: AI Scoring and Ranking Engine
description: Scores each verified opportunity against the organisation profile with the 100-point weighted model, applies disqualifier caps deterministically, ranks the pipeline and asks a human whether to pursue.

steps.name: Load opportunity, profile and criteria
steps.description: Read the Opportunity, the organisation profile (config/organisation-profile.json, updated from uploaded documents) and config/scoring-criteria.json.

steps.name: AI assessment
steps.description: Produce per-criterion sub-scores with a reason each, plus eligibility assessment, strengths, weaknesses, missing requirements and disqualification risks. Sub-scores must respect each criterion maximum and the rubric. Unverified organisation facts (verified=false) must be treated as unconfirmed and lower confidence.

steps.name: Compute total deterministically
steps.description: Validate sub-scores against the criteria file, sum them, apply the disqualifier cap (39) if any hard disqualifier is present and assign the band. The model-reported total is ignored. Implemented in src/lib/scoring.js.

onError.note: Invalid or out-of-range sub-scores trigger one regeneration.

steps.name: Save score and update opportunity
steps.description: Append an OpportunityScore history record and copy the latest summary to Opportunity.score.

steps.name: Rank and notify
steps.description: Recompute the ranked list. If total >= minimumScoreToNotify (65), send an internal Notification with the recommended next action.

steps.name: Human decision: pursue or archive
steps.description: A human reviews the score card and chooses Pursue, Enquire first, Monitor or Archive. Pursue sets the status to pursue_approved. This is an internal decision gate; nothing is sent externally.

aiInstructions.systemPrompt: You are a grants and business development analyst for {{organisation.tradingName}}. Score the opportunity using the supplied rubric. Use ONLY facts present in the supplied context (organisation profile, uploaded documents, retrieved page text). If a fact is missing, output null or a [[NEEDS_INPUT: description]] marker. Never invent credentials, statistics, URLs, deadlines or funding amounts. Be conservative: if eligibility depends on a document or fact the organisation has not verified, score lower and list it under missingRequirements.
guardrails: Do not copy the funder's marketing language into strengths; cite concrete matches.
List every possible disqualification risk, even unlikely ones.
aiInstructions.outputFormat: JSON: { subScores{key:number}, eligibilityAssessment, strengths[], weaknesses[], missingRequirements[], disqualificationRisks[], disqualifiers[], recommendedNextAction, reasons{key:string} }

output.description: Score card: overall score, band, eligibility assessment, strengths, weaknesses, missing requirements, disqualification risks, recommended next action.

onUnrecoverableFailure: Set the run status to "failed" and stop; never continue past a failed safety check.
Write a WorkflowLog entry with level "error" and the failing stepId.
Send an internal alert to INTERNAL_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL (internal only; never to external recipients).
errorHandling.idempotency: Every run carries a runId. Writes use natural keys (fingerprint, draftId, followUpId) so a retried run cannot create duplicates or send twice.

specificCases.action: Regenerate once; if still invalid mark the run failed and leave the opportunity "verified".
Proceed but add the caveat "scored against unverified organisation data" to the score card.

approval.rationale: A person decides whether to invest preparation effort. No external action occurs.

logging.redaction: Never log credentials, OAuth tokens or full email bodies. Log IDs and content hashes instead.

base44.automation: Entity automation on Opportunity status = verified.
base44.notes: Executable reference logic: src/lib/scoring.js with unit tests in tests/scoring.test.js.
